name: wolfbook
description: Mathematica-style Wolfram Language notebooks and WPaper LaTeX editing in VS Code, with live kernels, compiled-paper navigation, rich output, debugging and agent tools.

cellUri.description: URI of the notebook cell to debug (auto-filled)

wolfbook.localTheme.description: Local workspace style. Choose Wolfbook: Local Theme to select a light, dark, or automatically adapting accent. Notebook backgrounds are independent. Store this in Workspace settings.

appearance.description: Follow the active VS Code theme, or select a matching light/dark base theme in this workspace.

enumDescriptions: Auto-detect: changed cells use Refine mode, unchanged cells use Advance mode
Always advance: scroll to output and move focus to next cell after every evaluation
Always refine: no scroll, no focus change — stay on the same cell in edit mode
wolfbook.evalMode.description: Post-evaluation scroll and focus behaviour. Auto detects whether the cell changed since last run.

wolfbook.editor.autoReplaceUnicode.description: Automatically replace \[Name] with Unicode characters as you type

wolfbook.timeout_warning_enabled.description: Enables the timeout warning if the kernel does not start after 15 seconds

wolfbook.systemKernel.markdownDescription: Path to the Wolfram kernel executable, or `Automatic` to use the first detected installation. Run the **Wolfbook: Select Kernel** command (`wolfbook.selectKernel`) to pick from all detected kernels.

wolfbook.activeSystemPrompt.markdownDescription: Name of the active @wolfbook system prompt preset (matches a file in `~/.wolfbook/prompts/<name>.md`). Set per-workspace so different projects can use different prompt styles. Change via **Wolfbook: Notebook Settings** → Copilot Instructions.

wolfbook.mcpEnabled.markdownDescription: Enable the MCP (Model Context Protocol) server so Claude and other MCP agents can connect to this window's Wolfbook tools. Disable to prevent external agent connections. Requires window reload to take effect.

wolfbook.mcp.canonicalOutputProjection.markdownDescription: Preview the versioned canonical notebook projection through MCP: source, plain/LaTeX previews, and MIME/hash manifests without persisted renderer HTML. Does not change .wb files. Requires reload.

wolfbook.mcp.renderCache.markdownDescription: Allow the canonical MCP projection to cache derivable rendered HTML in the extension global-storage content-addressed cache. Never writes cache data into notebooks. Requires reload.

wolfbook.mcp.boundedResults.markdownDescription: Replace large MCP text responses with a preview and expiring result handle retrievable through wolfbook_getResult. Requires reload.

wolfbook.mcp.resultHandleThreshold.markdownDescription: Character threshold for bounded MCP result envelopes.

wolfbook.mcp.requireToken.markdownDescription: Require Wolfbook's per-user access token (`~/.wolfbook/mcp-token`) from every local program that connects to the MCP server over TCP. The stdio bridge and Wolfbook's own windows send it automatically, so configured agents need nothing. It stops other user accounts and sandboxed apps from running code through Wolfbook. Turn off only for a client that connects by URL and cannot send an `Authorization` header.

wolfbook.mcp.announceNewAgents.markdownDescription: Show a one-time notice (with a **Block** button) the first time a new AI agent connects to Wolfbook. Never blocks the agent. Manage agents with **Wolfbook: Manage Agent Access**.

wolfbook.mcp.profile.markdownDescription: Which tools the MCP server lists. `auto` (default): the frequently used tools always, slide and paper tools while a `.wslide` deck or `.tex` paper is open in any Wolfbook window, and anything else on demand — agents call `wolfbook_tools` to list families and enable them. `economy`: the smallest notebook workflow with compact schemas. `notebook`, `slides`, `paper`: fixed legacy subsets. `full`: everything. Every tool stays callable by name. Requires reload.

wolfbook.mcp.exposeDeprecatedTools.markdownDescription: Advertise deprecated MCP tool names (tagged `mcp:deprecated`) in tools/list with a DEPRECATED prefix. When off, the names still work when called directly but are not listed. Requires reload.

wolfbook.ai.busyPolicy.markdownDescription: Policy when an AI tool requests the Wolfram kernel while another evaluation is running. `reject` preserves the running work and returns structured busy status. `preempt` restores legacy AI-priority behavior and must also be explicitly requested by the tool call.

wolfbook.remote.allowHostExtension.markdownDescription: Allow the **Wolfbook Remote Host** companion extension (`wolfbook.wolfbook-remote-host`) to drive this window via the `wolfbook.remote.*` command surface. Each workspace also requires a one-time consent prompt the first time the host extension connects. Set to `false` to disable the remote bridge entirely.

wolfbook.remote.checkpointDirectoryName.markdownDescription: Subpath inside the notebook's `.img/` sidecar directory where `wolfbook_remote_checkpoint` files are written. Each notebook gets its own checkpoint history; the agent reads back prior checkpoints via standard file tools.

wolfbook.remote.mirrorWolfbookToolUsage.markdownDescription: Forward Wolfbook MCP tool invocations (run cell, edit cell, etc.) to paired iOS devices via the Wolfbook Remote Host as a live activity timeline. Disable to keep tool usage local.

wolfbook.collabMode.markdownDescription: Enable Collab mode: the AI agent works in a right-column split editor while the user keeps focus in the left editor. Agent cell reveals and highlights appear in the right pane without disturbing the user's cursor or scroll position.

wolfbook.copilotPrePromptPresets.markdownDescription: Named pre-prompt presets for the @wolfbook chat participant. Each key is a preset name, value is the pre-prompt text.

wolfbook.advanced.lsp.ServerLogDirectory.description: Directory for the Wolfram LSP server log

wolfbook.advanced.diagnosticLogs.description: Write diagnostic logs (btl.log, ai_eval_log.md, wolfram-kernel-debug.log, wstp.log). Off by default. When enabled, logs go to the extension's global storage — never beside your notebooks, so they are not synced by Dropbox/iCloud.

wolfbook.advanced.telemetryRetainRuns.description: How many Oberon telemetry run logs to keep. Older runs are pruned at startup. Set to 0 to keep everything (unbounded growth).

wolfbook.advanced.lsp.command.description: Command to start the Wolfram LSP server

wolfbook.lsp.implicitTokens.description: Experimental option for the Wolfram LSP server

wolfbook.lsp.semanticTokens.description: Experimental option for the Wolfram LSP server

wolfbook.lsp.ignoreUnicodeCharacters.description: Ignore Unicode characters in LSP diagnostics (e.g., Greek letters like α, β, γ)

wolfbook.editor.globalSymbolColor.description: Color applied to Global` context symbols (user-defined variables). Leave empty or set to 'auto' for automatic theme-aware color (#7eb3d4 on dark themes, #333333 on light). Set to 'off' or 'none' to disable. Accepts any CSS color string.

wolfbook.notebook.rendering.invertBright.description: When an expression is evaluated, this option specifies whether the brightness of the images in the output should be inverted in dark and high contrast themes.

wolfbook.notebook.rendering.interactive3.markdownDescription: Attach interactive 3D data to `Graphics3D` outputs. The picture still renders as a static image — dragging it turns it into a rotatable WebGL view, and the **3D** output button opens it directly. Turn off to skip the extra work (roughly 70–200 ms per 3D output) if you never rotate plots.

wolfbook.notebook.rendering.plotTooltips.markdownDescription: Show a coordinate callout when hovering the curves of a 2D plot, the way Mathematica's `PlotHighlighting` does. The picture itself is unchanged; this only writes a small curve-data file next to it. Turn off to skip that work.

enumDescriptions: PNG image (default, compatible with all outputs)
Genuine HTML export like Wolfram Cloud
MathML for native mathematical notation
Plain text InputForm (flattened boxes)

wolfbook.notebook.rendering.lineBreaking.description: Automatically wrap long mathematical expressions (WLLatex mode) across multiple lines based on the notebook container width.
Base font size in pixels used by line-break iteration when pageWidthPx is provided.
Indentation step (in spaces) used after line breaks.
Maximum recursion depth for delimiter-internal line breaking.
Maximum refinement iterations when pixel-width line breaking is enabled.
Use compact multiline layout in line-broken output.

wolfbook.notebook.rendering.trigOmitPare.description: Omit parentheses around a single-symbol trig argument: \sin(\phi) → \sin\phi.

wolfbook.notebook.rendering.trigPowerFor.description: Move the exponent onto the trig command when the base is a parenthesised trig expression: (\sin\phi)² → \sin²\phi.

wolfbook.formatter.pageLength.description: Target line width for the Wolfbook WL code formatter. Default: 150.

wolfbook.formatter.replaceNamedChars.description: When formatting, replace \[Name] escape sequences with their UTF-8 Unicode characters (e.g. \[Alpha] → α).

wolfbook.formatter.replaceMultiply.description: When formatting with Option+Shift+F (UTF mode), replace explicit * multiplication operators with implicit multiplication (a space), e.g. a*b → a b. Preserves *= (TimesBy). Off by default; always enabled in UTF format mode.

wolfbook.formatter.autoFormat.description: Automatically format the current cell when Enter is pressed (new line). Disabled by default.

wolfbook.notebook.textOutput.pageWidth.description: Maximum line width when exporting notebook output to a text (.wls) file via 'Open as text'

wolfbook.notebook.print.pageWidth.description: Kernel $PageWidth for Print[] output (characters per line). Default 156 = 2× the Mathematica default of 78.

wolfbook.notebook.appearanceByUri.markdownDescription: Legacy per-user notebook appearance map. Wolfbook now migrates these values into workspaceState so multiple notebooks persist locally without modifying the shared `.wb` file.

wolfbook.kernels.experimentalIsolation.markdownDescription: Legacy compatibility setting. Explicit private kernels are now available by default; kernel slots and notebook bindings are restored after reload, and definitions are never copied between kernels.

wolfbook.kernels.maximum.markdownDescription: Recommended number of local Wolfram kernels in one window. Advisory only: explicit creation may exceed it. Prefer reusing a kernel associated with your repository; each additional process consumes memory and may need a license seat.

wolfbook.kernels.defaultForNewNotebooks.markdownDescription: Kernel for new, unassigned notebooks in this workspace. Choose **Use Wolfram … for new notebooks in this workspace** in the notebook's kernel status menu. The value is a durable kernel slot (`default` for the window's shared kernel), not a runtime kernel ID or label. Empty asks on the first keyboard evaluation. Explicit notebook assignments and agent kernel/isolation choices take precedence; an unavailable chosen kernel is never silently replaced.

wolfbook.oberon.enabled.markdownDescription: Enable the Oberon research-agent layer. **Experimental.** Guarded execution — not a full security sandbox. Trusted local use only.

wolfbook.oberon.showControlRoom.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Show the Oberon **Control Room** view in the activity bar. Parked by default while Oberon is under development — use **🧚 Fairy quick compute** in the main Wolfbook (Watch) panel instead. Reload the window after changing.

wolfbook.oberon.experimentalPipeline.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Run the full Oberon pipeline (Skeptic critic + Oberon report) after the Fairy. When off (default), **🧚 Fairy quick compute** runs a minimal Fairy only — faster, no critic, no report. Toggle from the **Oberon** switch in the Wolfbook (Watch) panel.

wolfbook.oberon.providers.deepseek.apiKe.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** DeepSeek API key for the Oberon research agent. **Setting a key is what enables Oberon — with no key configured it never runs and sends nothing anywhere.** Runs cost real money (typically a few cents each; see `#wolfbook.oberon.budgets.run#` for the ceilings). Prefer `apiKeyEnv` to read the key from an environment variable rather than storing it in settings.
**Experimental.** Environment variable to read the DeepSeek API key from. Used when `apiKey` is empty.

wolfbook.oberon.providers.deepseek.timeo.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Per-request timeout in milliseconds for DeepSeek calls. On streaming calls this bounds time-to-first-byte only — a live stream is guarded by the SSE stall detector instead. Raise it if long reasoning-model calls (deepseek-v4-pro) time out.

wolfbook.oberon.providers.openai.apiKey.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** OpenAI API key (sk-…). Stored in user settings; prefer `apiKeyEnv` for env-based loading.

wolfbook.oberon.providers.openai.apiKeyE.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Environment variable name to read the OpenAI API key from when `apiKey` is empty.

wolfbook.oberon.providers.openai.baseUrl.description: **Experimental.** OpenAI API base URL (override for compatible gateways).

wolfbook.oberon.providers.anthropic.apiK.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Anthropic API key (sk-ant-…). Stored in user settings; prefer `apiKeyEnv` for env-based loading.
**Experimental.** Environment variable name to read the Anthropic API key from when `apiKey` is empty.

wolfbook.oberon.roles.oberon.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Supervisor (Oberon) model binding. `maxTokens`: max output tokens per LLM call (default 12000; increase further for very complex Quests). `contextWindow`: input context limit in tokens (informational). `pricing` values are USD per **million** tokens: `cacheMissUSDPerMTok` = cache-miss input rate, `cacheReadUSDPerMTok` = cache-hit input rate, `outputUSDPerMTok` = output rate. Use `null` for fields the provider does not report.

wolfbook.oberon.roles.fairy.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Default Fairy (worker) model binding. `maxTokens`: max output tokens per LLM call (default 12000). `contextWindow`: input context limit in tokens. `pricing` values are USD per **million** tokens.

wolfbook.oberon.roles.postmortem.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Optional override for the postmortem narrative model. Empty object = use `roles.fairy`.

wolfbook.oberon.roles.director.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Role binding for the **Oberon Director** (the planning/analysis layer above the Fairy): `{ "provider": "anthropic|openai|deepseek", "model": "...", "maxTokens": 8000, "pricing": {...} }`. Empty → falls back to the `oberon` role binding.

wolfbook.oberon.roles.slidewright.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Role binding for the **Wolfslide design assistant** (the on-canvas select-and-instruct co-designer): `{ "provider": "anthropic|openai|deepseek", "model": "...", "maxTokens": 1200, "pricing": {...} }`. Empty → falls back to the `fairy` role binding.

wolfbook.oberon.budgets.fairyDefault.description: **Experimental.** LEGACY — shown in the Control Room budget editor but NOT enforced by the live fairy loop (the loop budgets via `budgets.fairyFsm` and `budgets.run`). Kept for UI compatibility; will be removed when the Control Room editor migrates.

wolfbook.oberon.fairy.reasoning.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** **Selective thinking** for the fairy (DeepSeek V4). Auto-thinking is suppressed globally (it ran away unboundedly); these turns think deliberately: phase entries incl. the planning turn and every run_clean/polish decision (`onPhaseEntry`, default true), every `cadence` turns (default 5; `0` disables all selective thinking), and after `onFailureStreak` consecutive failed probes (default 2). `effort`: `medium` (default) | `high` | `max` — `low` is remapped (empirically pathological). `planner` (default true): the quest Planner call thinks at effort high.

wolfbook.oberon.budgets.fairyFsm.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** **Live per-Charm fairy budget** (passed into the fairy state machine; empty keys use the built-in defaults). Keys: `probe_budget` (60 — kernel probes per charm), `diagnose_probe_reserve` (3), `max_turns` (120 — LLM tool rounds), `max_backtracks` (3), `max_diagnose_turns` (6), `polish_run_clean_max` (6), `polish_turns_max` (12), `partial_report_turns_max` (6), `numeric_tol` (1e-10 — numeric check tolerance). Example: `{ "probe_budget": 20, "max_turns": 40 }` for cheaper runs.

wolfbook.oberon.budgets.run.description: **Experimental.** Hard per-RUN caps. When exceeded mid-run, Oberon emits a `budget.exhausted` event, aborts in-flight work, and the user still receives a low-confidence fallback Scroll. Set either field to 0 to disable that check.

wolfbook.oberon.toolLoopMultiplier.description: **Experimental.** LEGACY — NOT enforced by the live fairy loop (turn caps come from `budgets.fairyFsm.max_turns`). Kept for UI compatibility; will be removed when the Control Room editor migrates.

wolfbook.oberon.priceTablePath.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Optional path to a YAML price-table file that overrides the per-role pricing in `roles.*`. Empty = use role-embedded pricing.

wolfbook.oberon.telemetry.saveRawPrompts.description: **Experimental.** Persist raw outgoing prompts to .oberon/telemetry/blobs/. Off by default for privacy.

wolfbook.oberon.telemetry.saveRawRespons.description: **Experimental.** Persist raw model responses to .oberon/telemetry/blobs/. Required for replay/fork.

wolfbook.oberon.telemetry.redactSecrets.description: **Experimental.** Apply regex redaction to common API-key shapes before persisting blobs.

wolfbook.oberon.telemetry.retentionDays.description: **Experimental.** Number of days to keep raw blobs before pruning.

wolfbook.oberon.telemetry.maxBlobSizeMB.description: **Experimental.** Drop blobs larger than this size with a warning event.

wolfbook.oberon.telemetry.mirrorGlobalTo.description: **Experimental.** Debug: ingest ALL Wolfbook eventBus events into the active Oberon run, even uncorrelated ones.

wolfbook.oberon.mathematica.timeConstrai.description: **Experimental.** TimeConstrained wall-clock cap (seconds) for each Spell.

wolfbook.oberon.mathematica.guardMode.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Guarded-execution mode. **Not a full security sandbox** — see spec §9. `strict` blocks dangerous heads; `escalate` prompts the user; `off` runs anything (unsafe).

wolfbook.oberon.postmortem.narrativeEnab.description: **Experimental.** Generate a natural-language postmortem at the end of each run using the `postmortem` role (in addition to the deterministic metrics report).

wolfbook.oberon.git.autoCommitGrimoire.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Auto-commit Grimoire writes to the local workspace git repository (no push to remote, no notification).

wolfbook.oberon.recall.enabled.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** When enabled, Fairy searches SkilXiv before each run and presents a matching skill as reference material (RECALL phase). Fail-open — the core Fairy loop runs normally whether or not a skill is found.

wolfbook.oberon.recall.usageTelemetry.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** When enabled and a skill was consulted, a minimal usage event (skill ref, outcome, environment class — no task content) is submitted to SkilXiv. Confidential charms never submit usage events regardless of this setting.

wolfbook.oberon.recall.skilxiv.baseUrl.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Base URL for the SkilXiv registry API used by the RECALL phase.

wolfbook.oberon.contribution.mode.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Stage 2 contribution behaviour. `draft-on-approval` (default): after a delivered run with reusable results, a **local** contribution candidate is raised for your review — nothing is submitted until you explicitly approve it (creating a **private draft** under your SkilXiv account). `off`: never raise candidates. Submission is always human-approved; making a draft public is a separate step.

wolfbook.oberon.contribution.defaultLice.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Default license preselected in the contribution review dialog.

wolfbook.oberon.contribution.shareUsageP.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** When a run uses a recalled SkilXiv skill, a usage event is reported to confirm the skill worked. **Off (default):** the report is anonymous — only the aggregate success count is shown on the skill page, your identity is never exposed. **On:** your GitHub identity and a short, content-light agent report (task summary + key result, no notebook or raw query) may appear in the skill page's expandable run list. Aggregate counts are always anonymous regardless of this setting.

wolfbook.oberon.fairy.askSpecialistEnabl.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** When enabled (default), the Fairy agent can ask you a clarifying question via a VS Code input box when it is genuinely stuck. Disable to run fully autonomously without interruptions.

wolfbook.oberon.fairy.selfPostmortem.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Development feedback loop: right before the clean notebook is compiled (and on budget exhaustion), the Fairy writes a structured self-postmortem — what it achieved, where it struggled, which tools helped or were missing, and concrete recommendations. Shown as a cell in working.wb, saved to the charm folder as `self_postmortem.md`, and emitted as telemetry. One extra cache-warm LLM call per run.

wolfbook.oberon.fairy.askSpecialistTimeo.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Maximum time a Fairy question may block a run. On timeout it continues with its best evidence.

wolfbook.oberon.fairy.askSpecialistMaxPe.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Maximum specialist dialogs per Charm. Near-duplicate questions reuse the first result.

wolfbook.oberon.fairy.rejectRedefinition.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** When enabled (default), the Fairy agent is blocked from re-pasting a definition for a symbol already alive in the kernel (a registered util or a recorded step). This forces incremental, step-by-step calculation instead of rebuilding from scratch. A probe may deliberately redefine a symbol by including a leading `(* redefine: symbolName *)` comment. Disable to allow unrestricted redefinition.

wolfbook.oberon.notebookFirstExecution.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** When enabled (default), Oberon creates a live `.wb` charm notebook before the Fairy's first LLM turn so computation progress is visible in real time. Disable to run in kernel-only mode (no live notebook) — useful for testing or when VS Code notebook APIs are unavailable.

wolfbook.oberon.executive.autoDispatch.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** When enabled, Oberon's executive-analysis follow-up briefs (`decompose_further`, `retry_subset`, `extract_and_continue`, `reformulate_brief`) are auto-dispatched as a new research run without waiting for the user to click *Run Oberon Follow-up*. Bounded by `executive.maxAutoFollowups` to prevent unbounded chains.

wolfbook.oberon.executive.maxAutoFollowu.description: **Experimental.** Maximum recursion depth for auto-dispatched executive follow-ups. 0 disables auto-dispatch even if executive.autoDispatch is on.

wolfbook.oberon.executive.maxPerQuest.description: **Experimental.** Maximum number of executive analyses Oberon may run within a single Quest (across failing Charms).

wolfbook.oberon.director.maxStages.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Director: maximum fairy stages per programme (1–12).

wolfbook.oberon.director.maxReplans.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Director: maximum plan mutations (revise/insert/drop) per programme.

wolfbook.oberon.director.maxLitConsults.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Director: maximum literature consults per programme.

wolfbook.oberon.director.maxAskUser.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Director: maximum questions to the human per programme (0 = fully autonomous).

wolfbook.oberon.director.maxUSD.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Director: per-programme cost cap in USD (replaces the per-run budget for Director runs). A 15% reserve is kept for synthesis + report.

wolfbook.oberon.director.compilePdf.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Director: try to compile report.tex to PDF with pdflatex (best-effort; the .tex is always written).

wolfbook.oberon.director.skillCandidate.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Director: raise a SkilXiv skill candidate when the synthesis judges the result considerable and novel (goes to the review inbox; never auto-submits unless autoSubmitSkill).

wolfbook.oberon.director.autoSubmitSkill.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Director: auto-submit the authored skill draft to SkilXiv when signed in (default off — drafts wait in the review panel).

wolfbook.oberon.director.stageContinuati.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Director: fairy budget continuations auto-granted per stage (no dialogs).

wolfbook.oberon.memory.extractPartialFac.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Extract `verified:false` working facts from non-success Scrolls (confidence ≥ 0.4) into project memory, so future Charms in the same Quest do not redo partially-completed work.

wolfbook.oberon.replay.perCellTimeoutSec.description: **Experimental.** Per-cell timeout (seconds) used by replayNotebook when re-evaluating a Charm notebook after a kernel restart (revision or Skeptic kernel-busy recovery).

wolfbook.tex.enable.markdownDescription: Enable WPaper: outline, folding, CodeLens and deterministic diagnostics for `.tex` files, plus the `paper_*` agent tools. Wolfbook deliberately does **not** contribute a `latex` language or grammar, so it coexists with LaTeX Workshop rather than competing with it. Requires reload.

wolfbook.tex.diagnostics.markdownDescription: `semantic` reports unresolved `\\ref`, duplicate `\\label`, unbalanced environments and managed-block states — all computed without a compiler, so they are safe on the keystroke path. Compile errors stay with LaTeX Workshop. `off` disables them.

wolfbook.tex.codeLens.markdownDescription: Show `Ask · Find refs · Copy key` above equations, figures and tables, and the state of each managed `%Mathematica` block.

wolfbook.tex.compile.markdownDescription: When to build the render map. `onSave` compiles the paper out-of-tree after each save (typing is never blocked; a large paper takes ~15 s). `manual` compiles only via **Wolfbook: Compile WPaper**. `off` disables compiling entirely — the structural outline and diagnostics still work.

wolfbook.tex.engine.markdownDescription: Engine passed to `latexmk`. Compiles run **out of tree** in a temp directory, so your project is never written to; a `.latexmkrc` in the project is still honoured.

wolfbook.tex.compileTimeoutMs.description: Maximum compiler run time in milliseconds for a WPaper build, including optional WLaTeX previews. A fallback compiler receives its own time limit. Does not include source synchronization or map loading.

wolfbook.tex.mapEngine.markdownDescription: How WPaper builds its render map. `auto` (default): when `lualatex` is installed, the WPaper view is compiled with LuaLaTeX plus the wbmap hook, so every printed glyph is mapped to its exact box and source line (exact click-to-source and cursor highlight); a document LuaLaTeX cannot build falls back to `#wolfbook.tex.engine#` with an approximate (SyncTeX) map. `lualatex`: always. `wlatex`: use a separately installed WLaTeX engine: the page follows every keystroke through its incremental engine, and its native build settles the paper (index, glossaries, BibTeX and biber included); saves stay native unless that build left a tool pending, and an explicit Compile uses the configured engine. Configure `#wolfbook.tex.wlatexDirectory#` or WLATEX_HOME. If WLaTeX is unavailable, use the normal automatic map engine. `off`: never — use `#wolfbook.tex.engine#` and SyncTeX only.

wolfbook.tex.wlatexDirectory.description: Optional absolute path to a separate WLaTeX installation or built development checkout. WLATEX_HOME is used when empty. WLaTeX is not bundled with WPaper; if unavailable, WPaper uses its existing compiler.

wolfbook.tex.review.historyLimit.description: Maximum recent external versions retained in WPaper History per paper. Older versions are discarded when the paper is opened or a review is saved. 0 disables version history. Pending corrections, the approved baseline and review feedback are preserved.

wolfbook.tex.review.historyMaxMB.description: Maximum combined size in MiB of the before/after texts retained in WPaper History per paper. The oldest versions are discarded first; historyLimit also applies. 0 disables version history. Active corrections and saved approvals are independent of this budget.

wolfbook.tex.review.groupWindowSeconds.description: How close together two writes from an agent must be to count as ONE arrival in the review. An agent rewrites the same paragraph two or three times in a row; grouping them keeps the list about the paper rather than about the writes, and interrupts you once per episode instead of once per write. 0 groups nothing.

wolfbook.tex.liveRender.description: Recompile the paper from the unsaved editor buffer shortly after you stop typing, so the WPaper view keeps up without a save. The .tex file on disk is never written.

wolfbook.tex.liveRenderDelayMs.description: The LONGEST Wolfbook will wait after the last keystroke before a live recompile. Papers that rebuild quickly recompile sooner: the wait tracks how long the last live rebuild actually took, so a fast paper feels immediate while a long one stays calm.

wolfbook.tex.livePreviewThrottleMs.description: With the WLaTeX engine: how long a burst of keystrokes is merged before the incremental engine redraws the page (a newer request abandons an older one at its next page).

enumDescriptions: Overleaf's Git integration: every few minutes, while you pause, WPaper commits your changes, merges collaborators' and pushes. Needs the project's Git remote and an Overleaf Git authentication token (a paid Overleaf plan). Overleaf's tracked changes and comments on lines a push changes can be lost or displaced.

Real-time editing, as a collaborator in the Overleaf editor: the paper's folder is linked to an Overleaf project and edited in place, signed in with your browser's Overleaf session cookie. NOT supported by Overleaf: its terms forbid access other than through its supported interfaces, so this can break at any time and use of it is at your own risk (and your account's). Off unless you choose it.
No Overleaf synchronisation: commit and push yourself.
wolfbook.tex.overleafSync.description: How a paper that lives on Overleaf is kept in step with it.

wolfbook.tex.overleafSyncMinutes.description: Overleaf auto-sync (Git): how often, in minutes, your changes are committed and pushed and collaborators' merged in. Overleaf rate-limits frequent Git polling.

wolfbook.tex.nativeSettleDelayMs.description: With the WLaTeX engine: how long typing must pause before the full native build settles the paper (PDF, cross-references, every page's source map). The live page does not wait for it.

wolfbook.tex.inspireSearch.description: WLaTeX Pro: the citation picker (⌘⇧C at the page caret) also searches INSPIRE-HEP (inspirehep.net) for what you type — words, an arXiv number or a texkey — and a record you choose is added to the paper's .bib (or its thebibliography). Only the typed search is sent.

wolfbook.tex.inkTyping.description: WLaTeX Pro: a click on prose puts a caret on the page itself, and typing edits the LaTeX there (what you type is what shows: % becomes \%; Backspace never breaks a command). A click in maths opens the equation card (Mathematica's keys), in a table the table grid, on a picture its figure's card. Escape puts the caret away.

wolfbook.tex.trackMyChanges.description: WLaTeX Pro: each change you make on the page (typing in the ink, the edit card, tables, figures, moves and drops) shows in the review, to keep or undo, as an agent's changes do. Typing in the editor is not tracked. Also a checkbox in the WLaTeX Pro panel.

wolfbook.tex.synctex.description: With the WLaTeX engine: also write SyncTeX for external PDF viewers (Skim, Zathura, SumatraPDF). Export PDF then saves a .synctex.gz with absolute source paths beside the exported file. WPaper's own viewer does not need it.

wolfbook.tex.shellEscape.markdownDescription: With the WLaTeX engine: let papers run shell commands (`\write18`, as `-shell-escape` does), for packages such as `minted` or TikZ externalization. **The commands run with your rights**, so only turn this on for papers you trust. It is a user setting only (a workspace cannot turn it on), applies in trusted workspaces, and affects the full builds; the live preview never runs commands.

wolfbook.tex.liveSinglePass.description: While you type, run a single LaTeX pass instead of the full rerun loop. This is what makes a long paper repaint in a moment rather than a minute. Cross-references, the table of contents and page numbers can lag briefly; a full rebuild runs when you pause or save and corrects them.

wolfbook.tex.authoritativeDelayMs.description: How long after the last keystroke to run the full rebuild that converges cross-references. 0 turns it off, leaving saving as the moment things converge. Always sits behind the live rebuild.

enumDescriptions: Viewer-only: WPaper replaces the .tex tab and the second editor group closes; nothing else changes.
Also put the VS Code window into operating-system full screen for the viewer-only step.
Use Zen Mode for the viewer-only step, hiding the status bar and tabs too.
wolfbook.tex.fullScreenMode.description: How the viewer-only step of WPaper’s three-state layout cycle is displayed. The button cycles through viewer only, viewer + agent panel, and editor + viewer + agents; Esc restores the complete layout.

wolfbook.tex.lockViewerGroup.description: Lock the editor group the WPaper view opens in, so clicking a file or a search result does not open it on top of the paper.

wolfbook.tex.viewerFollowsTex.description: Close the WPaper view when the editor group beside it switches to a file that is not a .tex, and bring it back — at the same place — when you return to one. Panels, terminals and agent sessions never close it.

enumDescriptions: Follow the VS Code colour theme: dark themes darken the pages.
Always show the paper on white, as it will be printed — even in a dark theme.
Always darken the pages.
wolfbook.tex.pageTheme.description: How the compiled pages are shown in the WPaper view. Darkening inverts the rendered image, so figures and photographs invert with it; the toolbar's sun/moon button switches this without opening settings.

wolfbook.tex.hoverRender.markdownDescription: When hovering a `\ref`/`\eqref`, also show the target **as it prints** — a fragment clipped from the compiled page — beneath its source. Needs the WPaper view to be open; the hover falls back to source only when it is not.

enumDescriptions: The reference as it would normally be written: \eqref{eq:foo} for an equation, \ref{fig:bar} otherwise, \cite{key} for a citation.
Just the name: eq:foo.
Always \ref{...} (\cite{...} for citations).
Always \eqref{...} (\cite{...} for citations).
wolfbook.tex.labelCopyFormat.markdownDescription: What clicking a label chip in the WPaper view puts on the clipboard. Hold Shift over the page to reveal the labels; **Alt-click** a chip copies the other of bare/command, so the setting never has to be visited mid-flow.

wolfbook.tex.inverseClickCaret.markdownDescription:
When you click a word in the WPaper page, put the editor's caret at the **character you clicked** and outline the word, instead of selecting the whole word. VS Code's caret can only sit at one end of a selection, so a selected word cannot show where in it you pointed.

Turn this off to restore the older behaviour (the word selected, caret at its end) — useful if you click a word in order to type over it. **Double-click still selects the word** either way, and ⌘/Ctrl-click still selects the widened group.

wolfbook.notebook.highlightRunningLines.markdownDescription:
While a cell runs, outline it in gold and gently shade the **lines currently being evaluated** rather than the whole cell. A cell is sent to the kernel one top-level expression at a time, so on a long cell this shows where the computation has got to.

Neither mark moves or blinks — they are found once and then ignored. Both disappear when the cell finishes, however it finishes.

wolfbook.keybindings.notebook.markdownDescription:
Enable Wolfbook's keyboard shortcuts inside Wolfram notebooks (`.wb`, `.vsnb`, `.evsnb`) — Shift+Enter to evaluate, the arrow-key cell navigation, bracket wrapping, Escape-mode aliases, and the rest.

Turn this off to keep your own bindings and use the Command Palette instead. Shortcuts in other file types are unaffected.

wolfbook.keybindings.tex.markdownDescription:
Enable Wolfbook's keyboard shortcuts in `.tex` files — smart paste, Alt+[ / Alt+] to step through an agent's changes, Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+Enter to commit, and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Alt+Enter to push.

Paper-view gestures are gated on the **WPaper viewer being open**; Git commit/push remains available in an ordinary `.tex` editor. Turn this off to disable them entirely.
